sources.title: CreateProcessW
sources.fact: Explicit executable, handle/environment rules and initialization boundary; process creation does not establish readiness.

sources.title: Named pipe security
sources.fact: Named pipes support security descriptors and access checks; default permissions are not the proposed least-privilege policy.

sources.title: Overlapped pipe I/O
sources.fact: Overlapped pipe operations require completion handling and per-operation state; pending return is not completed work.

sources.title: CancelIoEx
sources.fact: Cancellation requests do not wait for completion; operations may complete normally, cancel or fail.

sources.title: GetProcessTimes
sources.fact: Creation time uses FILETIME; exit-time contents are undefined before exit, and query rights are required.

sources.title: WaitForSingleObject
sources.fact: Process waits require synchronization rights; closing a waited handle is undefined, and low-power timeout behavior differs by Windows version.

sources.title: TerminateProcess
sources.fact: Termination of another process is asynchronous; a request is not independent proof of completed exit.

sources.title: QPC timing guidance
sources.fact: Same-machine comparisons are supported subject to documented limitations; cross-thread differences within one tick have ambiguous ordering.

sources.title: Process security and rights
sources.fact: Creation returns a broad process handle; query, synchronization and termination rights differ and should be separated.

sources.title: DuplicateHandle
sources.fact: Handle duplication supports explicit rights/inheritance; same-access duplication ignores requested narrower rights.

sources.title: Job objects
sources.fact: Job lifetime and process grouping have separate behavior; this design does not select or configure a Job Object.

sources.title: Named pipe creation flags
sources.fact: Named-pipe flags include rejecting remote clients and overlapped operation; this is documentation, not an endpoint created here.

sources.title: Pipe client PID
sources.fact: API retrieves the pipe client's process ID, not complete ownership or creation-time proof.

sources.title: Pipe server PID
sources.fact: API retrieves the pipe server's process ID, not authenticated role or retained-handle provenance.

sources.title: PROCESS_INFORMATION process-object and identifier lifetime
sources.fact: A retained process handle keeps its process object and identifier alive. Numeric identifier reuse is unavailable in the selected retained-handle replacement variant; it is not merely unlikely.
